headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared MCP/IO pathways; no direct evidence of blocking isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so dbt-core outputs could be bridged into it and treated as instructions. dbt-core can call a data warehouse and has allowlisted egress, while OpenBBTerminal uses a 'connect once, consume everywhere' pattern. No direct isolation or provenance controls are documented, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF dbt-core output is forwarded into OpenBBTerminal via MCP or stdin/stdout, injection is possible.
IF OpenBBTerminal parses upstream text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents.
Route dbt-core output through a strict JSON schema validator.
Strip executable-looking text before handing data to OpenBBTerminal.
Require human review for any instruction-like content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data. OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so if dbt outputs are passed through those channels, sensitive warehouse data can leak into a third-party-facing context. The profiles do not show filesystem isolation or explicit redaction, so the risk is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs warehouse rows into OpenBBTerminal inputs, leakage can occur.
IF OpenBBTerminal forwards received context to external APIs, the shared data may exit the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not pass warehouse rows directly into OpenBBTerminal.
Redact identifiers and secrets before transfer.
Use a one-way export file with minimal columns.
Turn off external API calls during shared workflows.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and data-warehouse API access, while OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem write, no shell, and no git modification. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited. The only plausible conflict is on shared external APIs or MCP endpoints, which is narrower than the rubric's medium threshold.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable MCP endpoint, conflicts can arise.
IF dbt-core and OpenBBTerminal share a writable external resource, last-writer-wins behavior may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Avoid shared mutable endpoints.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Monitor for conflicting updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP servers, so it may treat dbt-core outputs as authoritative inputs for downstream financial analysis or actions. dbt-core produces warehouse-derived outputs, and OpenBBTerminal's 'connect once, consume everywhere' pattern increases the chance of unverified propagation. No built-in verification step is documented, so cascading errors are plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes dbt-core outputs without validation, errors can propagate.
IF downstream workflows act on those outputs, incorrect warehouse facts can affect financial decisions.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require source-of-truth checks for key fields.
Mark dbt outputs as untrusted until verified.
Limit downstream actions to read-only analysis.
requires-engineering: add automated reconciliation tests.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP/REST APIs. If warehouse data includes regulated or restricted records, moving it into OpenBBTerminal can create retention, licensing, or residency mismatches. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated or restricted records, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF OpenBBTerminal logs or forwards received data, retention or residency rules may be violated.
mitigations: Classify the data before transfer.
Exclude regulated rows from shared workflows.
Review logging settings in OpenBBTerminal.
Keep licensed data separate from warehouse exports.
requires-engineering: document a joint retention policy.
